name: confirm holds a Replace Patch and passes a Replace Current Patch
about: A Circuit patch SysEx whose byte 6 is 01 writes flash and is held until a person confirms it, while one whose byte 6 is 00 lands in RAM and passes.
notes: Circuit patch SysEx starts F0 00 20 29 01 60, and byte 6 (counting F0 as byte 0) is the command: 01 Replace Patch writes flash, 00 Replace Current Patch is RAM.
The bodies here are shortened. A real patch message is 350 bytes. The gate reads only the head.
circuit's profile: sysex allow, clock deny, and one rule, a SysEx starting F0 00 20 29 01 60 01 is confirm. Rules are byte prefixes and the first matching rule wins over the per kind policy.
bare has no profile, so it gets the default: allow for everything except sysex, which is confirm.
SysEx may arrive in chunks. A chunk that does not start with a status byte continues the open SysEx from the same port, and the gate's decision on the first chunk holds for the whole stream.
t 0 and t 1: a Replace Patch in two chunks. Held at circuit by the rule, held at bare by the default. Nothing out.
t 2: a note passes to both while the SysEx is held. Link order: l1 circuit, then l2 bare.
t 3: a Replace Current Patch, whole. circuit allows it. NEGATIVE CONTROL: bare holds it, because the default for an unknown port is confirm.
t 4: clock. NEGATIVE CONTROL: circuit denies it and it is dropped. bare allows it.
t 5: confirm circuit. The held stream is released in its chunks, at the confirm's time. bare is not touched.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 6: a second Replace Patch is held again at circuit, because a confirm is once per action and not forever.
End: circuit holds 1 stream, bare holds 3 (the t 0 stream, the t 3 message and the t 6 message).
